question: Which of the following options represents the number of neutrons present in aluminium?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**14**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The number of **neutrons** in an element can be calculated using the formula: **Neutrons = Mass Number - Atomic Number**.
 
• **Aluminium (Al)** has an **atomic number** of **13** and a **mass number** of **27**.
 
• Using the formula: **Neutrons = 27 - 13 = 14**.
 
• Hence, Aluminium has a total of **14 neutrons**.
 
• The **atomic number** represents the number of **protons** in an element, which is equal to the number of **electrons** in a neutral atom.
 
• The **mass number** is the sum of the number of **protons** and **neutrons** in the nucleus.
 
• **Aluminium** is a widely used metal known for its **lightweight**, **non-corrosive**, and **ductile properties**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **15**__

 __
 
• The value **15** does not correspond to the number of neutrons in Aluminium.
 
• It is important to correctly subtract the **atomic number from the mass number** to avoid errors.
 
 
 
• **27**__
 __
 
• **27** is the **mass number** of Aluminium, not the number of neutrons.
 
• The mass number includes the total number of **protons and neutrons** in the nucleus of an atom.
 
 
 
• **13**__
 
 
• **13** is the **atomic number** of Aluminium, representing the number of **protons** or **electrons** in a neutral atom.
